questions.question:
The standard deviation of the set {10, 11, 9, 11, 9}

A. 1/√5

B. 2/√5

C. 3/√5

D. 0
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

For a set x1, x2, ..., xn of n observations:

 
• Mean: bar{x} =dfrac{x₁+x₂+ ... +xₙ}{n}.
 
• Variance: sigma² =dfrac{(x₁-bar{x})²+(x₂-bar{x})²+...+(xₙ-bar{x})²}{n}=dfrac{sum (x_i-bar x)²}{n}=dfrac{sum x_i²}{n}-bar x².
 
• Standard Deviation: sigma=sqrt{sigma²}=sqrt{Variance}.

**Calculations:**

Average of the numbers = (10 + 11 + 9 + 11 + 9)/5 = 10

We get,

(10 – 10)² = 0

(11 – 10)² = 1

(9 – 10)² = 1

(11 – 10)² = 1

(9 – 10)² = 1

∴ Standard deviation of the set = sqrt {frac{{0 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1}}{5}} = (2)/({sqrt 5 )}

• Methane emissions also result from livestock and other agricultural practices and by the decay of organic waste in municipal solid waste landfills.

**Nitrous oxide (N₂****O)**:

 
• Nitrous oxide is emitted during agricultural and industrial activities, combustion of fossil fuels and solid waste, as well as during the treatment of wastewater.

 

**Fluorinated gases:**

 
• Hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulfur hexafluoride, and nitrogen trifluoride are synthetic, powerful greenhouse gases that are emitted from a variety of industrial processes.

questions.question:
An 18 feet high electric pole is located along a 6 feet tall tree at a distance of 10 feet from. What will be the length of the tree's shadow?

A. 10 feet

B. 7.5 feet

C. 6 feet

D. 5 feet
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio of heights** of the **pole** and the **tree** is 18 : 6 = 3 : 1.

In **similar triangles**, the ratio of their total distance from the shadow tip to the shadow length must be the same: (10 + s) : s = 3 : 1.

Using the **unitary method**, if 3 parts = 10 + s and 1 part = s, then the difference (2 parts) = 10 feet.

Since 2 parts = 10 feet, then 1 part (shadow length s) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 feet.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 feet.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Height of **electric pole** (H) = 18 feet, Height of **tree** (h) = 6 feet, **Distance** between pole and tree (d) = 10 feet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c4943410325e08fa97c34b1ed02540b5a53683d22947eeddb41f5d7653ccaa0.png] 

The **light ray** from the top of the pole passes the top of the tree to form the **shadow**, creating two **similar triangles**.

⇒ (Height of Pole) ÷ (Total Distance from Pole to Shadow Tip) = (Height of Tree) ÷ (Shadow Length)

⇒ 18 ÷ (10 + s) = 6 ÷ s

⇒ 18 × s = 6 × (10 + s)

⇒ 3s = 10 + s

⇒ 3s − s = 10

⇒ 2s = 10

⇒ s = 5 feet

**∴ The correct answer is 5 feet.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

Two triangles are **similar** if their corresponding angles are equal; their **corresponding sides** are always in the same **ratio**.

Shadow Length Formula

For objects sharing the same **elevation angle** of a light source: (Object Height₁ / Shadow Length₁) = (Object Height₂ / Shadow Length₂).

Thales Theorem

Also known as the **Basic Proportionality Theorem**, it states that a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.</p
